findings.locator: Leo XIII Libertas §§30–35, especially §34 on public welfare and tolerance
findings.document_finding: Leo XIII differentiates moral truth from a State's prudent toleration of wrongful acts; tolerance is constrained by public welfare.
findings.qualification: A doctrine of governmental toleration alone does not answer every question about civil immunity.

findings.locator: Vatican II Dignitatis humanae §§1–2, due limits and immunity from coercion
findings.document_finding: The declaration grounds civil immunity from coercion in personal dignity, including public and collective religion subject to due limits.
findings.qualification: Civil immunity is not a positive doctrinal assertion that rival religions teach the same truth.

findings.locator: SSPX 2012 authorial objection, explicit four alleged doctrinal discontinuities
findings.document_finding: The Society names DH §2 and the earlier Magisterium as a central contradiction, rather than merely disliking dialogue.
findings.qualification: This documents the objection's authorship, not its magisterial validity.

findings.locator: SSPX General House, Religious Liberty, civil State neutrality objection
findings.document_finding: The original institutional objection concerns State duties regarding false public worship as well as individual freedom.
findings.qualification: The criticism must be answered alongside the declaration's just-public-order restrictions.

findings.locator: SSPX USA 2012 'Is the SSPX heretical?' first and subsequent parts
findings.document_finding: The named four topics are DH §2, LG §8, UR §3 and LG §22; the author states continued attachment to Roman authority.
findings.qualification: Objections to doctrinal content are not archival evidence that the Council was unlawfully constituted.

findings.locator: CDF 2007 Responses, questions 2–5 on identity and incomplete communion
findings.document_finding: The CDF denies multiple fully equal subsistences, describing one concrete Catholic Church with ecclesial elements beyond.
findings.qualification: This official account does not independently answer all four of the SSPX's published issues.

findings.locator: Pius XI Mortalium animos §§6–10, condemnation of federated pan-Christianism
findings.document_finding: Pius XI objects to a federation whose members retain incompatible dogmas and forbids Catholics joining those schemes.
findings.qualification: The scope is the enterprises he describes, not a line-by-line assessment of every later dialogue.

findings.locator: Vatican II Unitatis redintegratio §§3–4, imperfect bonds and ecumenical cooperation
findings.document_finding: The decree recognises Christian realities in separated communities while assigning unity's fullness to Catholic communion.
findings.qualification: This does entail changed permitted contacts, which must not be denied as if practice were identical to 1928.

findings.locator: Pius XI Mortalium animos §9, all revealed dogmas require equal assent of divine faith
findings.document_finding: Pius XI specifically rejects classification of divine revelations into articles mandatory and dispensable for belief.
findings.qualification: Equal obligation of faith is not equivalent to an identical pedagogical ordering of dogmas.

findings.locator: Vatican II Unitatis redintegratio §11, hierarchy of truths
findings.document_finding: The hierarchy concerns doctrine's varied relation to foundational Christian faith, not permission to disbelieve a revelation.
findings.qualification: The text does not by itself regulate every ceremony of interconfessional prayer.

findings.locator: Lumen gentium §§14 and 16, knowingly refusing necessity versus nonculpable ignorance
findings.document_finding: LG distinguishes deliberate rejection by a person who knows Catholic necessity from people unaware without personal fault.
findings.qualification: No individual person's final subjective state can be conclusively inferred from visible membership alone.

findings.locator: Dominus Iesus §§20–22 on salvation, mission and the Church
findings.document_finding: The CDF refuses autonomous salvation outside Christ's universal mediation and retains missionary obligation.
findings.qualification: This must not be interpreted as the conclusion that all non-Catholics are personally culpable.

findings.locator: Catechism §§839–848 on Jewish ties, mission and Church necessity
findings.document_finding: The Catechism places objective need for the Church alongside non-culpable ignorance and God's freedom.
findings.qualification: Reference identifies doctrinal distinction but does not certify each pastoral inference.

findings.locator: St Paul Romans 11:1–2, 17–24, 28–29
findings.document_finding: Paul rejects the claim God abandoned Israel, forbids Gentile boastfulness and says the gifts and call are irrevocable.
findings.qualification: Scriptural claims must not be collapsed into the proposition that all later religious systems teach Christ identically.

findings.locator: Hebrews 8:6–13, new covenant in Christ contrasted with prior order
findings.document_finding: Hebrews names Christ mediator of the better covenant and uses Jeremiah's new-covenant prophecy.
findings.qualification: The text does not provide a simple ethnographic description of contemporary rabbinic practice.

findings.locator: Nostra aetate §4, Jewish calling, the Passion and racial and collective accusations
findings.document_finding: The declaration rejects collective Jewish guilt and antisemitism while affirming Christ's salvific work.
findings.qualification: The source does not establish the truth of every modern rabbinic doctrine.

findings.locator: Martin Stepanich, 2009 una cum Benedicto article, republished CMRI
findings.document_finding: Stepanich treats una cum prayer as a communion question and warns against attending Masses naming the pope he rejects.
findings.qualification: Original issuer page and publication context located; full text not independently collated page by page.

findings.locator: Bishop Mark Pivarunas, CMRI, My Thoughts in Regard to the Una Cum Issue, including 2002 statement
findings.document_finding: Pivarunas says attendance is not automatically mortal sin and cites CMRI permission to petition sacraments from some una cum clergy.
findings.qualification: Proponent page and indexed excerpt reviewed; further exact paragraph and edition collation remains open.

findings.locator: CDF Communionis notio §§13–16 on visible hierarchical communion
findings.document_finding: Visible ties with Roman Pontiff and bishops are constitutive of ecclesial communion.
findings.qualification: The CDF letter is not an ad hoc ruling about every modern una cum case.

findings.locator: CDF 1998 Professio fidei doctrinal commentary, three concluding doctrinal categories
findings.document_finding: The authentic commentary defines revealed, definitively held and non-definitive authentic teaching and due assent.
findings.qualification: Classification of a particular new instruction still requires its actual intended authority.

findings.locator: Donum veritatis §§23–31, non-irreformable magisterial teaching
findings.document_finding: The CDF both requires loyalty to authentic teaching and acknowledges possible difficulties.
findings.qualification: The source should not be misused to demand blind silence or to authorise an unconditional veto.

findings.locator: 1983 Code canon 212 §§1–3, obedience, petitions and the faithful's expression of views
findings.document_finding: The canon gives rights and sometimes duties subject to reverence, faith and common good.
findings.qualification: Its pastoral requirements do not confer a lay private universal teaching jurisdiction.

findings.locator: Donum veritatis §30, loyal theological dialogue in difficulties
findings.document_finding: The instruction recognises substantive non-definitive difficulties and counsels disciplined consultation.
findings.qualification: It does not establish that every public campaign of dissent is an appropriate form of correction.

findings.locator: SSPX 2012 actual objection to Unitatis redintegratio §3
findings.document_finding: The Society expressly identifies ecumenism among four alleged conciliar doctrinal discontinuities.
findings.qualification: That identification alone does not establish Catholic teaching abolishes conversion.

findings.locator: CDF Responsa 2007 Q4–Q5, true Eastern Churches vs ecclesial communities
findings.document_finding: The CDF distinguishes valid orders and Eucharist in the Eastern Churches from Protestant ecclesial communities lacking apostolic orders.
findings.qualification: The authority distinguishes objective ecclesial structures and does not judge individual souls.

findings.locator: Pius XI Mortalium animos §§6–10, condition of full unity and prohibition of specified projects
findings.document_finding: Pius XI forbids pan-Christian projects that compromise doctrine and calls separated believers to unity.
findings.qualification: Source supports actual historical discipline; it cannot stand in place of Unitatis redintegratio text.

findings.locator: Unitatis redintegratio §§3–4, 11 on dialogue and hierarchy of truths
findings.document_finding: The Council endorses ecumenism but retains integrity of Catholic faith and the fullness of means of salvation.
findings.qualification: Whether a later shared rite violated Catholic worship rules is case specific.

findings.locator: SSPX 2012 published Lumen gentium §8 alleged contradiction
findings.document_finding: The Society directly alleges the ecclesial subsistence formula ruptures earlier Church teaching.
findings.qualification: This is an institutional theological claim, not an undisputed interpretive fact.

findings.locator: CDF Responsa 2007 Questions 1–5, subsistit in and ecclesial status
findings.document_finding: The CDF claims unique enduring identity in the Catholic Church and distinguishes Eastern Churches and Protestant communities.
findings.qualification: Official Roman exposition documents a contrary account without automatically refuting every prior argument.

findings.locator: CDF 2007 original explanatory commentary, unique nonmultipliable subsistence
findings.document_finding: The commentary specifically says the word subsistit does not pluralise the one Church's historical identity.
findings.qualification: The explanatory text must be weighed with the Council and prior Magisterium for final doctrinal adjudication.

outstanding: Original Italian/Latin ecclesial-magisterial source edition collation and published proponent corpus remain necessary for theological approval.
For CMRI/Stepanich una cum positions, an issuer source and excerpts are located but exact complete first-person texts were not independently collated; status is documented accordingly.

The 1928/1964 differences in permission for ecumenical encounters require study of later competent liturgical norms; showing a changed practice does not itself establish a formally contradictory dogma.

The Catholic interpretation of unique subsistit is documented in 2007 CDF Response and Commentary, while the SSPX 2012 objection remains an actual competing published contention requiring reasoned analysis.
Bilingual French text was revised but has not undergone independent native-language editorial approval; all 141 canonical dossier publication flags remain false.
